To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of a SLAM system is best measured by the accuracy of the trajectory that it produces, that this accuracy should be computed using relative relations between poses rather than global positions, and that the accuracy can be computed using only the corrected poses and their covariances.
We propose a novel metric for measuring the accuracy of a SLAM algorithm based on relative pose information only.
the accuracy of a SLAM solution is best measured by computing the error between the estimated trajectory and a ground truth trajectory.

the following questions: How can we measure the accuracy of a SLAM algorithm? How can we compare different SLAM algorithms? What are the most suitable datasets to compare SLAM algorithms?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accuracy of a SLAM system depends on the type of environment in which it is applied.
our benchmark framework provides a new, easy and objective way to compare SLAM approaches and to analyze the results.
the SLAM community needs a benchmarking fram ework to objectively compare different SL AM algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method is an objective and easy-to-use framework for evaluating the performance of a SLAM algorithm.
we have created a new metric for SLAM error evaluation, and we have provided a framework to compute the metric for a number of datasets.
our method is a metric to evaluate SLAM algorithms, it is not an algorithm to perform SLAM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the error metric proposed in this paper is a more appropriate measure for SLAM than the commonly used metric based on the global frame.
the accuracy of SL AM approaches can be evaluated in an objective and fair manner.
the performance of different SLAM approaches is highly dependent on the type and the size of the dataset used to evaluate them.
